Visit note | 2025-07-29 02:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Sanjay Sen, 80, male. Mr. Sen returns for review, reporting that his symptoms are worse at night, with a burning sensation in both feet and numbness in his toes. He mentions this has been worse since walking barefoot at home in Sylhet. He works as a homemaker and denies any recent injuries or back pain. On examination, reduced sensation at 6 of 10 monofilament test sites is noted, along with other vitals: BP 122/74 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 83 kg. Examination of the lower limbs shows symmetric sensory loss in a stocking distribution with absent ankle jerks. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. A prescription was issued. He was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-07-30 10:00 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Sharmin Bepari, 48, female. Mrs. Bepari presents for a review of her endocrine status, reporting symptoms of a racing heart and shaky hands. She states that these manifestations were first noticed when her clothes became loose during an extended stay in Mymensingh. She works as an office cleaner and has no prior documented chronic medical illnesses. She denies any prior history of thyroid disorders, heat intolerance, or visual changes. Upon clinical examination, her pulse is elevated at 119 beats per minute, while other recorded vitals include a blood pressure of 127/76 mmHg and a total body weight of 85 kg. General physical examination reveals fine tremors of the outstretched fingers and warm, moist skin, although the cardiovascular examination is otherwise unremarkable with regular rhythm despite the tachycardia. Examination of the neck demonstrates a diffuse, non-tender enlargement of the thyroid gland without palpable nodules or audible bruits. Systemic review of the chest and abdomen yields normal findings with no evidence of cardiac failure or peripheral edema. Assessment of the clinical and objective findings leads to the diagnosis of Hyperthyroidism. A prescription was issued today to manage her condition. The patient received detailed lifestyle counseling, being specifically advised to avoid excess consumption of tea and coffee and to ensure adequate rest whenever her heart races. Follow-up appointment is scheduled in 4 weeks alongside repeat thyroid function tests to monitor her treatment response.
